_schema.what: An external ground truth for the land pattern a package is supposed to have. verify.py compares the geometry footprints.py generates against this file. The file exists so that the claim 'this footprint is correct' has a place to live that is not the code that makes the footprint.

fields.pad_count: Number of copper pads. Checked exactly against the generated footprint.
fields.pitch_mm: Pad centre-to-centre pitch, when the package has one repeating pitch. null to skip.
fields.row_mm: Row-to-row spacing for two-row packages (DIP/SOIC). null to skip.
fields.source: Where the numbers came from. Empty string means nobody has supplied an external figure yet.
fields.verified: true only when source names a real, checked figure (datasheet table, IPC-7351B, KiCad library). false = self-declared.

_schema.how_to_use: Add or correct an entry when a part's real land pattern is established. verified:true is a person's claim and should name its source exactly. Until then the check reports 'evidence/unknown', never 'pass'.
_schema.why_not_more: Rung IV of the verification tree. No free tool checks pin numbering or land geometry against a real part; the strongest honest claim available in software is 'the code matches a figure we wrote down', which is not the same as 'the figure is right'.

_note_on_provenance: Every entry below is verified:false. The pad counts and pitches are read back from footprints.py's own comments and geometry, so they confirm the code is self-consistent and nothing more. Setting verified:true requires an external figure for that specific package.
_table_note: exception_to_footprints_py: where an entry's numbers disagree with footprints.py, the check FAILS and names the package. That is the point — the table is written to be able to disagree.
